key_insight: Human hearing appears to form a continuous five-dimensional coordinate system rather than discrete hearing “types,” and the Human Hearing Atlas can reconstruct audiograms with near-decibel accuracy.
clinical_relevance: This could enable more precise hearing phenotyping, tracking of subtle within-ear changes, and better stratification for otology research, genetics, epidemiology, and clinical trials.
method: Integrated 33 datasets across 8 countries and 62 years
Tested whether hearing patterns are discrete types or continuous states
evidence_signal: The abstract reports validation across more than 4.29 million audiograms, with reconstruction of unseen audiograms to near-decibel accuracy and preservation of clinical detail.
watch_item: The atlas may depend on consistent audiogram calibration and dataset quality, so external validation and implementation standardization will be important.
paper_title: The Human Hearing Atlas: a canonical map of human hearing
